newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call eases, govt securities rally continues.
newsitem.headline: Indian call eases, govt securities rally continues.

text.p: Indian overnight call rates dipped to 2.75-3.25 percent in late Thursday morning trade from 3.5-4.0 percent opening on easy liquidity, dealers said.
An ongoing rally in government securities propelled by excess liquidity in the banking system was unabated, they said.
The rally was particularly evident in long-term papers.
"The 12.59 percent 2004, which has become a bell-wether stock, is up 40 paise at 105.03 rupees today," a dealer said.
The market has taken the four-year paper auction scheduled for July 28 in its stride, dealers said.
"There was a minor sell-off for 10 minutes when it was announced," a dealer said. "Cautious buying resumed the same evening."
Some dealers said some primary dealers and big buyers had massively undercut at the last auction on July 16.
"We were all caught on the wrong foot. It would be difficult to forecast the cut-off this time until the afternoon of Monday," said a dealer, referring to the July 28 auction.
At the July 16 auction of a six-year paper, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) set a cut-off rate of 11.83 against market expectations of 11.90/95 percent, dealers said.
